      "slideIndex": 1,
      "title": "Freshness determines whether a response can be reused; validation determines whether it must be checked",
      "section": "HTTP caching",
      "titleRegister": "claim",
      "keyPoints": [
        "Cache-Control establishes freshness policy: max-age and s-maxage define reuse windows, while public and private control who may store a response.",
        "no-cache permits storage but requires validation before reuse; no-store prevents storage; must-revalidate restricts serving a stale response once the response is no longer fresh.",
        "ETag supplies a representation validator: the client or intermediary sends If-None-Match, and the origin can return 304 Not Modified when the representation is unchanged.",
        "A 304 response reuses the cached body while updating applicable metadata; it is a bandwidth-saving check, not a directive that makes content fresh indefinitely."
      ],
      "suggestedLayout": "Two Column",
      "contentType": "twoColumn",
      "notes": "Use two tightly structured panels: left for Cache-Control directive semantics and right for the ETag/If-None-Match request-response flow. Include a small annotated HTTP example in the lower portion of the right panel."
    },
    {
      "slideIndex": 2,
      "title": "A CDN may serve stale content only when an explicit stale policy or failure mode permits it",
      "section": "HTTP caching",
      "titleRegister": "claim",
      "keyPoints": [
        "Normal behavior is to serve a fresh cached response; after expiry, the CDN should revalidate or fetch a new representation before serving it.",
        "stale-while-revalidate permits serving stale content while the CDN revalidates asynchronously, trading immediate freshness for lower latency.",
        "stale-if-error permits stale delivery when revalidation or origin retrieval fails, limiting availability impact during upstream errors.",
        "Absent an applicable stale directive or provider-specific rule, stale content should not be treated as automatically deliverable; inspect Age, Warning, response headers, and CDN behavior when debugging."
      ],
      "suggestedLayout": "Title and Content",
      "contentType": "content",
      "notes": "Close with a compact decision path: fresh hit -> serve; stale with permitted background revalidation -> serve and revalidate; stale with permitted error fallback -> serve on failure; otherwise -> revalidate or fetch. Keep the discussion provider-neutral and grounded in HTTP semantics."
    }
  ],
  "deviations": []
}
